note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-21). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. Biblical people named in the chapter (Cain, Balaam, Korah, Enoch, Michael) are not portrayed and nothing violent is shown.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: Job was a man of integrity whose full and blessed life went together with a father's watchful care for his children before God.
ideas: A grey-haired man bows his head in thanks at the head of a long harvest table crowded with his grown children and workers, his fields and herds behind
A man stands on his farmhouse porch at golden evening with his big family round him and pastures full of animals behind
A farmer leans on his gate at sunrise looking out over a flourishing farm that runs to the horizon
A shopkeeper runs after a customer to give back the extra change he was overpaid
At first light a father stands praying at a table still strewn with his grown children's party of the night before
Before dawn a father kneels by a window praying, framed photographs of his children on the sill
A father lies awake late at night with the porch light on until the last of his children's cars comes home
A father watches from a hilltop as the lit windows of his children's houses glow across the valley
A full barn at harvest with every stall and loft filled
A man's weathered hands hold a heavy basket of fruit from his own orchard

sections.meaning: The good man is noticed, and the question is put: does anyone fear God for nothing, or only for what he gets, so his faith will be tested by losing everything.
ideas: In a windswept field of bent, crooked trees one tall straight oak stands upright
A jeweller studies a single flawless stone under a loupe in bright light
A farmhouse ringed on every side by a tall thick hedge, green and lush inside, bare and dry outside
A dog trots obediently at a man's heel, its eyes fixed only on the bag of treats in his hand
A child hugs a visiting uncle while staring at the present in his hands
A gap has opened in the hedge round the farmhouse and a dark storm is rolling toward it
A goldsmith holds a crucible of molten gold in the heart of the furnace flame
A blacksmith plunges a glowing blade into water to test it
A climber's rope is loaded with a heavy weight to see whether it will hold
A bridge has a line of heavy trucks driven onto it to test its strength

sections.meaning: Loss falls upon loss without a pause, each blow arriving before the last has been told, until even his children are gone.
ideas: A man in his farmyard turns as one breathless worker runs up to him, a second already running down the road behind and a third far off
A man opens his front door to a dusty farmhand with a stricken face, cap in hand
Lightning splits the sky over a hillside pasture where the grass burns in a long line of flame
A barn burns at night while a farmer watches far off with his hands on his head
A big corral stands empty at dusk, its gate hanging open and the ground churned with hoofprints
A farmer stands alone in an empty paddock holding an empty halter
A storm has torn the roof off a house and a long table laid for a celebration stands with empty chairs under the grey sky
An old man's hands hold a family photograph in a cracked frame in a storm-wrecked room
A row of dominoes falls one after another
A telephone rings and rings on a kitchen table while another rings in the hall

sections.meaning: Stripped of everything, Job falls down and worships: we come with nothing and go with nothing, the Lord gave and has taken, blessed be his name.
ideas: A grey-haired man kneels with his forehead to the floor of a bare emptied room in quiet dawn light
A man kneels in a burnt empty field at sunrise, his face lifted and his hands open
An old man's open empty hands, palms up, lifted toward a bright morning sky
A newborn's tiny hand curls round an old man's finger
A man stands in the ruins of his house with his head bowed and his hand on his heart
Empty hands let a handful of sand run out into the wind
A man walks away from a ruined farm toward the sunrise, empty-handed and upright
An empty cradle beside an empty chair in morning light
A man sets the one cup left to him on the table and gives thanks
The tide carries away footprints on a beach at dawn

candidates.prompt: At a long wooden table set outdoors beside a farmhouse at golden evening, a big family of grown sons and daughters and farm workers sit together over a harvest meal. At the head of the table a grey-haired man in a plain shirt bows his head in thanks, and everyone round the table has bowed with him. Behind them wide green pastures full of grazing sheep and cattle stretch away to the hills.

On the porch of a large, well-kept farmhouse at golden evening, a strong grey-haired man stands with his arms round two of his grown children, and the rest of a big family of sons and daughters are gathered round him laughing. Beyond the porch rail, wide green pastures full of sheep and cattle stretch away under a warm sky, and farm hands are bringing the herds home.

At first light a grey-haired father stands with his head bowed and his hands folded in prayer at the end of a long table still strewn with the remains of his grown children's party the night before: empty glasses, candles burnt down, chairs pushed back. The pale blue dawn shows in the window behind him. The house is quiet.

Before dawn, in a quiet room lit only by one small lamp, a grey-haired father kneels at a window with his hands clasped and his head bowed in prayer. On the window sill in front of him stand a row of framed photographs of his grown sons and daughters. Outside the window the sky is just turning pale.

A wide open field on a windswept hill under a clear sky. Every tree in the field has been bent and twisted crooked by the wind, leaning low. In the middle stands one tall oak, perfectly straight and upright, green and strong, the only one of its kind. Clear daylight picks it out.

A close view in bright clean daylight at a jeweller's bench: the jeweller's eye is pressed to a loupe as he holds a single clear, flawless gemstone up in fine tweezers, studying it with great care. The stone sparkles brilliantly. His face and the stone are sharp, the bench softly blurred.

Seen from a little above, a farmhouse with its barns, orchard and green fields is enclosed on every side by a tall, thick, unbroken green hedge. Inside the hedge everything is lush, flowering and fruitful, with cattle grazing. Outside the hedge the land all round is bare, dry and brown. Bright sunlight.

On a park path in bright daylight a man walks along, and a dog trots obediently at his heel, looking up eagerly. But the dog's eyes are fixed not on the man's face but only on the bag of treats in his hand. The man glances down at the dog with a thoughtful, questioning look.

In a dim workshop a goldsmith in a leather apron holds a small crucible of glowing molten gold with long iron tongs deep in the bright heart of a furnace flame. The gold shines white-hot. The firelight lights his intent face and the tongs. Everything else is dark.

Seen from a little above, a farmhouse in lush green fields is enclosed by a tall thick green hedge, but on one side a wide gap has been opened in the hedge. Through the gap, across the bare brown land outside, a huge dark storm front with rain and wind is rolling straight toward the house. The house is still in sunlight.

In a farmyard in daylight a grey-haired farmer turns in alarm as a breathless young worker runs up to him, dusty, his face stricken. Behind them, a second young man is already running down the farm road toward them, and a third, further off, is running too. The farmer's hand is raised to his mouth.

In bright daylight a grey-haired man has opened his front door to a dusty, out-of-breath young farmhand who stands on the step with his cap crushed in his hands and his face stricken with the news he brings. The man's face is just beginning to fall. Down the path behind the farmhand another young man is running toward the door.

A dark storm sky over a wide hillside pasture. A great fork of lightning strikes down from the clouds, and the dry grass of the pasture is burning in a long line of flame and smoke across the hill. The pasture is empty, with no animals and no people. The lightning and flames light the scene.

At dusk on a farm, far off across a field, a big wooden barn is burning with tall orange flames and smoke against the dark sky. In the foreground, seen from behind, a grey-haired farmer stands alone and still with both hands on his head, watching it burn. No one is in danger.

A large wooden corral on open farmland at dusk, utterly empty. Its gate has been torn open and hangs crooked on one hinge, and the dusty ground inside and out is churned with countless hoofprints all leading away toward the empty hills. No animal and no person anywhere.

A grey-haired farmer stands alone in the middle of a wide, empty paddock at dusk, holding an empty rope halter loosely in one hand and looking at it. The gate behind him stands open, and the fields all round are empty of every animal. His shoulders are bowed.

A family house after a great windstorm: the roof and one wall have been torn away, and the dining room stands open to a grey sky. In it a long table is still laid for a celebration, with plates, glasses and a cake, but every chair round it is empty and some are knocked over. Broken roof beams and leaves lie about. No people anywhere.

A close view of an old man's weathered hands holding a framed family photograph of his smiling grown sons and daughters. The glass of the frame is cracked across. Behind, softly blurred, is a room wrecked by a storm, with broken beams and grey daylight coming through the torn roof.

In a storm-damaged house open to a grey sky, a row of ten empty dining chairs stands along a long table covered in fallen leaves and dust. Wind has torn the curtains and broken the window. A single grey-haired man stands at the end of the table with his hand resting on the back of the nearest empty chair.

In a bare, emptied room in quiet dawn light, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt kneels and bows all the way down with his forehead to the wooden floor, his open hands resting on the floor beside his head, in worship. Soft light falls on him from a single window. The room has nothing else in it.

In a wide burnt and empty field at sunrise, with a ruined farmhouse far behind, a grey-haired man kneels on the ground, his face lifted toward the rising sun and his empty hands open at his sides in worship. The warm first light falls full on his face. He is calm.

A close view of an old man's weathered, empty hands, held open with palms up and lifted toward a bright morning sky full of soft golden light. Nothing is in them. Beyond them, out of focus, a wide open landscape at sunrise.

A close view in soft morning light of a newborn baby's tiny hand curled round the finger of an old man's weathered hand. Only the two hands are seen, against a soft plain blanket. Both hands are empty of anything else. Gentle and peaceful.
